2. Material facts for disposal of this appeal are that the appellants filed the aforesaid case before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka against the respondents for a declaration that notification dated 26-1-89 issued by respondent No. 1 promoting respondent No. 4 to the post of Administrative Officer in the Labour Directorate in supersession of the claim of the appellant was illegal and of no legal effect and also for a direction upon respondent Nos. 1 and 2 to reconsider the case of the appellant for promotion. The appellant's case, briefly, is that he was appointed steno-typist on 15-11-68 in the Directorate of Labour and on 6-11-74 he was appointed Stenographer-cum-Confidential Assistant temporarily on ad hoc basis in the same Directorate. Under a circular dated 10-7-82 the Establishment Ministry regularized his service as Stenographer (CA) with effect from 1-5-75 and in terms of the Enam Committee report dated 10-10-83 his post was declared as Stenographer (PA). In the Recruitment Rules 1983 published by the Labour Directorate in the official Gazette on 27-3-84 requisite qualification for the post of Administrative Officer of the Labour Directorate was 5 years-experience as Head Assistant or Stenographer-cum-Confidential Assistant. On 13-12-88 respondent No. 1 sent the names of 5 employees including that of the appellant in serial number 1 and that of respondent No. 4 in serial number 4 to the Public Service Commission for consideration for promotion to the post of Administrative Officer of the Directorate with the recommendation for same and except the appellant none completed 5 years-service in the feeder post but the Public Service Commission recommended the case of respondent No. 4 for promotion and accordingly he was promoted to the post of Administrative Officer by the impugned notification dated 26-1-89. The appellant's representation to respondent No. 1 and then appeal to the Government-respondent No. 2 having been dismissed, the case was filed before the Administrative Tribunal for the aforesaid reliefs. 

 12. It was argued in the said appeal that when the Chairman of the Board of Directors of Sonali Bank and other officials were made parties, there was a substantial compliance of the requirement of law even though the Sonali Bank was no doubt the employer of the appellant. It was argued that the respondents did not object to the joinder of the Sonali Bank as a party before the Administrative Tribunal taking upon themselves the full responsibility of the outcome of the litigation. 

 13. It was only at the appellate stage that the objection was taken and the technical error in the draftsmanship of the petition by a lawyer could have been conveniently corrected and the Appellate Tribunal could have conveniently read the cause title as Sonali Bank represented by the Chairman, Board of Directors thereof. The appellant further argued that the objection as to non-joinder of proper party was taken long 6 years after the case was filed and decided before the Administrative Tribunal and this conduct of the respondents was not noticed while dismissing the leave petition.
